To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

magnetic stimulation of cerebral cortex zones in post-apoplectics with mild or moderate motor dysfunction revealed reduced amplitude of the evoked response and prolonged central conduction on the paretic side; in post-apopletics with severe paresis magnetic stimulation of the affected hemisphere cortex did not evoke a response; and that in the early period after ischemic stroke, the degree of motor dysfunction is correlated with the degree of central motor conduction delay and the presence of M-response to magnetic cortex stimulation.

the complex of neurophysiological methods (magnetic stimulation of cerebral cortex, M-responses, and skin sympathetic potential) allows to assess the degree and type of motor disorders in patients with ischemic stroke in the early period after stroke.

magnetic stimulation of cerebral motor cortex and measurement of M-responses and evoked sympathetic potentials in postapoplectic patients can provide a more precise assessment of motor disorders than clinical examination alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early postapoplectic period, when clinical symptoms are not so pronounced, but the motor system is still in a state of functional reorganization.
the clinical and neurophysiological assessment of the recovery process in patients with ischemic stroke.
the complex clinico-electro-neurophysiological study of motor disorders in post-apoplectics in the early period following the ischemic stroke.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the early post- apoplectic period is characterized by a complex of motor disorders, the pathogenesis of which is determined by the degree of ischemic brain damage and the extent of the motor system involvement.
magnetic stimulation is an excellent method of neurophysiological investigation of the motor system in patients with ischemic hemispheral apoplexy.
the motor disorders in the early period after an apoplexy are associated with both peripheral and central pathogenetic mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early period of the recovery after stroke is a time of the dynamic processes in the brain and the nervous system, which are accompanied by the changes in the motor system functions.
the motor disorders in the postapoplectic period can be assessed by a complex neurophysiological approach.

a complex clinico-electro-physiological assessment of motor disorders in patients during early post-apoplectic convalescence allows to differentiate the severity of motor dysfunctions and to predict the course of their recovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in patients with mild or moderate motor dysfunction, the M-response amplitude is reduced, and the central conduction time in the pyramidal tract on the affected side is prolonged.
the motor disorders in post-apopletic patients during early convalecense are associated with a reduced amplitude and prolonged conduction of M-response and with no M-response in severe paresis.
the neurophysiological assessment of the early motor disorders in patients with ischemic stroke may help to improve the efficacy of the treatment.
